items.sourceEnglish: Plant Selection & Guilds
items.draft: Kgetho ya dimela le dihlopha tsa dimela (guilds)
items.blindBackTranslation: Selection of plants and plant groups (guilds)

items.sourceEnglish: Choose useful plant partners, return mulch and manage the guild as trees grow.
items.draft: Kgetha dimela tse thusanang, kgutlisetsa mulch mobung, mme o laole guild ha difate di ntse di hola.
items.blindBackTranslation: Choose plants that help one another, return mulch to the soil, and manage the guild as the trees grow.

items.sourceEnglish: These bacteria convert nitrogen from the air into forms the legume can use.
items.draft: Dibaktheria (bacteria) tsena di fetola nitrogen e tswang moyeng hore e be mefuta eo legume e ka e sebedisang.
items.blindBackTranslation: These bacteria change nitrogen from the air so that it becomes forms that a legume can use.

items.sourceEnglish: Find nodules on a spare legume plant. Nodulation and growth depend on the plant, suitable bacteria and growing conditions.
items.draft: Batla nodules ho semela sa legume seo o sa se hlokeng. Nodulation le kgolo di itshetlehile ka semela, dibaktheria (bacteria) tse loketseng le maemo a kgolo.
items.blindBackTranslation: Look for nodules on a legume plant that you do not [yet?] need. Nodulation and growth depend on the plant, the suitable bacteria and the growing conditions.

items.sourceEnglish: Return suitable leafy prunings, fallen leaves and crop residues as mulch. Soil organisms release nutrients during decomposition.
items.draft: Busetsa makala a nang le mahlaku a loketseng a faotsweng, mahlaku a wileng le masalla a dijalo e le mulch. Diphedi tsa mobu di lokolla nutrients nakong ya decomposition.
items.blindBackTranslation: Return branches that have suitable pruned leaves, fallen leaves and crop residues as mulch. Soil organisms release nutrients during decomposition.

items.sourceEnglish: This takes time. A living legume is not an instant fertiliser pipe into the fruit tree.
items.draft: Sena se nka nako. Legume e phelang ha se phaephe ya manyolo e yang sefateng sa ditholwana hang-hang.
items.blindBackTranslation: This takes time. A living legume is not a pipe of fertiliser that goes to the fruit tree immediately.

items.sourceEnglish: It is indigenous to KwaZulu-Natal. In suitable warm conditions, manage this short-lived shrub or small tree as a support plant.
items.draft: Ke semela se indigenous ho KwaZulu-Natal. Maemong a futhumetseng a loketseng, laola sehlahla sena se sa phelang nako e telele kapa sefate se senyane e le support plant.
items.blindBackTranslation: It is a plant indigenous to KwaZulu-Natal. In suitable warm conditions, manage this shrub that does not live a long time, or a small tree, as a support plant.

items.sourceEnglish: Allow room for its growth. Prune for mulch and reassess it when shade or water competition increases.
items.draft: Dumella sebaka bakeng sa kgolo ya sona. Faola bakeng sa mulch, mme o se hlahlobe hape ha moriti kapa tlhodisano ya metsi e eketseha.
items.blindBackTranslation: Allow space for its growth. Prune it for mulch, and check it again when shade or water competition increases.

items.sourceEnglish: Sesbania punicea is the invasive red sesbania. Its pods have four lengthwise wings. Confirm identity using reliable botanical guidance.
items.draft: Sesbania punicea ke red sesbania e invasive. Dikoko tsa yona tsa dipeo (pods) di na le mapheo a mane a tsamayang ka bolelele. Netefatsa hore ke sefe ka botanical guidance e tshepehang.
items.blindBackTranslation: Sesbania punicea is the invasive red sesbania. Its seed pods have four wings running lengthwise. Confirm which it is using reliable botanical guidance.

items.sourceEnglish: Check the full name before planting. Respect the agreed project species list, including any restriction on Sesbania sesban.
items.draft: Hlahloba lebitso le feletseng pele o jala. Hlompha project species list e dumellanweng, ho kenyeletswa thibelo efe kapa efe mabapi le Sesbania sesban.
items.blindBackTranslation: Check the full name before you plant. Respect the agreed project species list, including any restriction concerning Sesbania sesban.

items.sourceEnglish: Use a sunny, freely draining position. It is a short-lived support shrub; frost and waterlogging can limit it.
items.draft: Sebedisa sebaka se nang le letsatsi, se tswang metsi hantle. Ke support shrub e sa phelang nako e telele; serame le metsi a emeng di ka e fokotsa.
items.blindBackTranslation: Use a sunny, well-drained site. It is a short-lived support shrub; frost and standing water can reduce it.

items.sourceEnglish: Decide whether each plant mainly supplies peas or leafy material. Frequent severe cutting can damage it and reduce the food harvest.
items.draft: Etsa qeto ya hore na semela se seng le se seng se fana haholo ka dierekisi kapa ka thepa e nang le mahlaku. Ho seha ka makgetlo a mangata ka matla ho ka se senya le ho fokotsa thobo ya dijo.
items.blindBackTranslation: Decide whether each plant gives mainly peas or leafy material. Cutting hard many times can damage it and reduce food yield.

items.sourceEnglish: Cowpea covers sunny gaps. Pigeon pea provides food and leafy material. Managed Sesbania sesban can supply taller temporary support.
items.draft: Cowpea e kwahela dibaka tse bulehileng tse nang le letsatsi. Pigeon pea e fana ka dijo le thepa e nang le mahlaku. Sesbania sesban e laolwang e ka fana ka support plant e telele ho feta, ya nakwana.
items.blindBackTranslation: Cowpea covers open sunny areas. Pigeon pea provides food and leafy material. Managed Sesbania sesban can provide a taller, temporary support plant.

items.sourceEnglish: Add suitable flowering and mulch plants. Keep the mango trunk clear and manage light, water and access.
items.draft: Eketsa dimela tse loketseng, tse nang le dipalesa le tsa mulch. Boloka kutu ya sefate sa mango (trunk) e hlakile, mme o laole lesedi, metsi le tsela ya ho fihlella.
items.blindBackTranslation: Add suitable flowering plants and mulch plants. Keep the mango tree trunk clear, and manage light, water and access.

items.sourceEnglish: Count woody supports across the spaces between fruit trees. Sow suitable ground cover by area.
items.draft: Bala support plants tse nang le lehong ho pholletsa le dibaka tse pakeng tsa difate tsa ditholwana. Jala dimela tse loketseng tse kwahelang mobu ho ya ka sebaka.
items.blindBackTranslation: Count the woody support plants across the spaces between the fruit trees. Plant suitable ground-covering plants according to the area.

items.sourceEnglish: There is no universal number per fruit tree. Adjust density to water, soil, plant size and your ability to prune and thin.
items.draft: Ha ho na palo e tshwanang e sebetsang bakeng sa sefate se seng le se seng sa ditholwana. Fetola palo ya dimela ho ya ka metsi, mobu, boholo ba semela le bokgoni ba hao ba ho faola le ho fokotsa (thinning).
items.blindBackTranslation: There is no single number that works for every fruit tree. Adjust the number of plants according to water, soil, plant size and your ability to prune and thin.

items.sourceEnglish: Conceptual guild teaching illustration; confirm plant identity with reliable botanical guidance.
items.draft: Setshwantsho sa mohopolo sa ho ruta ka guild; netefatsa hore semela ke sefe ka botanical guidance e tshepehang.
items.blindBackTranslation: Concept picture for teaching about a guild; confirm which plant it is using reliable botanical guidance.

items.sourceEnglish: Nitrogen Fixers: Choose and Manage Support Plants
items.draft: Nitrogen fixers: ho kgetha le ho laola support plants
items.blindBackTranslation: Nitrogen fixers: choosing and managing support plants

items.sourceEnglish: Legumes work with rhizobia in root nodules; fixation depends on suitable conditions.
items.draft: Legumes di sebetsa mmoho le rhizobia ka hare ho nodules tsa metso; nitrogen fixation e itshetlehile ka maemo a loketseng.
items.blindBackTranslation: Legumes work together with rhizobia inside root nodules; nitrogen fixation depends on suitable conditions.

items.sourceEnglish: Return useful cut material to the soil; nutrient release takes time.
items.draft: Busetsa thepa e sehilweng e nang le molemo mobung; ho lokollwa ha nutrients ho nka nako.
items.blindBackTranslation: Return the cut material that has benefit to the soil; the release of nutrients takes time.

items.sourceEnglish: Use suitable seasonal cover, support shrubs and temporary trees.
items.draft: Sebedisa dimela tse kwahelang mobu nakong ya sehla tse loketseng, support shrubs le difate tsa nakwana.
items.blindBackTranslation: Use suitable seasonal ground-cover plants, support shrubs and temporary trees.

items.sourceEnglish: Manage support density as plants grow; there is no universal count per fruit tree.
items.draft: Laola support density ha dimela di ntse di hola; ha ho na palo e tshwanang e sebetsang bakeng sa sefate se seng le se seng sa ditholwana.
items.blindBackTranslation: Manage support density as the plants grow; there is no single number that works for every fruit tree.

items.sourceEnglish: When does nitrogen in cut legume material become available to other plants?
items.draft: Nitrogen e teng thepeng ya legume e sehilweng e fumaneha neng ho dimela tse ding?
items.blindBackTranslation: When does the nitrogen in cut legume material become available to other plants?

items.sourceEnglish: Immediately when it is cut
items.draft: Hang-hang ha e sehilwe
items.blindBackTranslation: Immediately when it is cut

items.sourceEnglish: As soil organisms decompose the material
items.draft: Ha diphedi tsa mobu di bodisa thepa eo
items.blindBackTranslation: When soil organisms break that material down

items.sourceEnglish: Only when the fruit tree touches the legume
items.draft: Feela ha sefate sa ditholwana se kgoma legume
items.blindBackTranslation: Only when a fruit tree touches a legume

items.sourceEnglish: It can never become available
items.draft: E ke ke ya fumaneha le ka mohla
items.blindBackTranslation: It will never become available

items.sourceEnglish: Decomposition releases nutrients over time. The rate depends on the material and growing conditions.
items.draft: Decomposition e lokolla nutrients ka nako. Lebelo le itshetlehile ka thepa le maemo a kgolo.
items.blindBackTranslation: Decomposition releases nutrients over time. The speed depends on the material and the growing conditions.

items.sourceEnglish: What should decide how many support plants you establish?
items.draft: Ke eng e lokelang ho etsa qeto ya hore na o theha support plants tse kae?
items.blindBackTranslation: What should decide how many support plants you establish?

items.sourceEnglish: The same fixed number at every site
items.draft: Palo e tshwanang sebakeng se seng le se seng
items.blindBackTranslation: The same number in every place

items.sourceEnglish: Water, soil, plant size and the care you can provide
items.draft: Metsi, mobu, boholo ba semela le tlhokomelo eo o ka fanang ka yona
items.blindBackTranslation: Water, soil, plant size and the care that you can give

items.sourceEnglish: Always placing every support uphill
items.draft: Kamehla ho beha support plant e nngwe le e nngwe ka lehlakoreng le phahameng la thaba (uphill)
items.blindBackTranslation: Always place every support plant on the higher side of the mountain/hill (uphill)

items.sourceEnglish: Planting as many trees as will physically fit
items.draft: Jala difate tse ngata kamoo sebaka se ka di amohelang ka teng
items.blindBackTranslation: Plant as many trees as the place can accept

items.sourceEnglish: Support plants need resources and management too. Observe growth and competition, then adjust.
items.draft: Support plants di hloka mehlodi le tlhokomelo le tsona. Hlokomela kgolo le tlhodisano, ebe o a fetola.
items.blindBackTranslation: Support plants need resources and care too. Watch growth and competition, then adjust.

items.sourceEnglish: The clip shows a branch cut: the support tree remains standing. Leave enough healthy foliage for the plant to recover.
items.draft: Video e bontsha lekala le sehilweng: support tree e ntse e eme. Tlohela mahlaku a lekaneng a phetseng hantle hore semela se fole.
items.blindBackTranslation: The video shows a pruned branch: the support tree remains standing. Leave enough healthy leaves so the plant recovers.

items.sourceEnglish: Match cutting to the species. Avoid frequent severe cuts on pigeon pea, especially when growing it for peas.
items.draft: Lekanyetsa ho seha ho ya ka mofuta wa semela. Qoba ho seha ka matla ka makgetlo a mangata ho pigeon pea, haholo-holo ha o e jala bakeng sa dierekisi.
items.blindBackTranslation: Adjust cutting according to the kind of plant. Avoid cutting heavily many times on pigeon pea, especially when you plant it for peas.

items.sourceEnglish: Mulch protects the surface, helps conserve moisture and returns organic material.
items.draft: Mulch e sireletsa bokahodimo ba mobu, e thusa ho boloka mongobo, mme e busetsa thepa ya organic.
items.blindBackTranslation: Mulch protects the surface of the soil, helps to keep moisture, and returns organic material.

items.sourceEnglish: Leave access for watering and inspection. Cut material into manageable pieces and keep observing moisture and decomposition.
items.draft: Boloka tsela ya ho fihlella bakeng sa ho nosetsa le ho hlahloba. Seha thepa dikotwana tse laolehang, mme o tswelepele ho shebisisa mongobo le decomposition.
items.blindBackTranslation: Keep an access path for watering and checking. Cut the material in manageable pieces, and continue to watch moisture and decomposition.

items.sourceEnglish: Obtain the correct cultivar. Bocking 14 does not spread by viable seed, but root pieces can regrow.
items.draft: Fumana cultivar e nepahetseng. Bocking 14 ha e phatlalale ka viable seed, empa dikotwana tsa metso di ka mela hape.
items.blindBackTranslation: Find a suitable cultivar. Bocking 14 ha is propagated by viable seed, but pieces of roots can grow again.

items.sourceEnglish: Place it where it has room and sufficient moisture. Cut leaves as it recovers; do not crowd the young fruit tree.
items.draft: E bee moo e nang le sebaka le mongobo o lekaneng. Seha mahlaku ha e ntse e fola; o se ke wa pitlaganya sefate se senyane sa ditholwana.
items.blindBackTranslation: Put it where there is space and enough moisture. Cut the leaves while it recovers; do not crowd the young fruit tree.

items.sourceEnglish: Many ladybirds eat aphids; some parasitoid wasps attack crop pests. Flowering members such as African basil can add resources.
items.draft: Ladybirds tse ngata di ja aphids; parasitoid wasps tse ding di hlasela dikokwanyana tse senyang dijalo (pests). Ditho tse nang le dipalesa tse kang African basil di ka eketsa mehlodi.
items.blindBackTranslation: Many ladybirds eat aphids; some parasitoid wasps attack insects that damage crops. Flowering members such as African basil can add resources.

items.sourceEnglish: Watch which insects visit and whether damage changes. A flowering plant does not guarantee pest control.
items.draft: Shebisisa hore ke dikokwanyana (insects) dife tse etelang le hore na tshenyo e a fetoha. Semela se nang le dipalesa ha se tiise ho laolwa ha dikokwanyana tse senyang (pests).
items.blindBackTranslation: Watch closely which insects visit and whether the damage changes. A flowering plant does not guarantee control of pests.

items.sourceEnglish: Tulbaghia violacea has narrow leaves and lilac flowers. Place a clump where it has light and room to grow.
items.draft: Tulbaghia violacea e na le mahlaku a masesane le dipalesa tse mmala wa lilac. Bea sehlopha sa yona moo se nang le lesedi le sebaka sa ho hola.
items.blindBackTranslation: Tulbaghia violacea has narrow leaves and lilac-coloured flowers. Place its clump where it has light and room to grow.

items.sourceEnglish: Observe visiting insects. Do not promise that a ring of wild garlic will repel pests or cure an outbreak.
items.draft: Shebisisa dikokwanyana (insects) tse etelang. O se ke wa tshepisa hore sedikadikwe (ring) sa wild garlic se tla leleka dikokwanyana tse senyang (pests) kapa hore se tla fedisa ho phatlalala ho kgolo ha tsona.
items.blindBackTranslation: Watch the visiting insects. Do not promise that a ring of wild garlic will repel pests or stop their spread and growth.

items.sourceEnglish: Conceptual guild teaching illustration; confirm plant identity with reliable botanical guidance.
items.draft: Setshwantsho sa mohopolo sa ho ruta ka guild; netefatsa hore semela ke sefe ka botanical guidance e tshepehang.
items.blindBackTranslation: Concept picture for teaching about a guild; confirm which plant it is using reliable botanical guidance.

items.sourceEnglish: Mulch Plants and Helpful Insects
items.draft: Dimela tsa mulch le dikokwanyana (insects) tse thusang
items.blindBackTranslation: Mulch plants and helpful insects

items.sourceEnglish: Pruning cuts branches while keeping the support plant.
items.draft: Ho faola ke ho seha makala ha support plant e ntse e sala.
items.blindBackTranslation: Pruning is cutting branches while the support plant remains.

items.sourceEnglish: Return suitable cut leaves as mulch while keeping the trunk clear.
items.draft: Busetsa mahlaku a sehilweng a loketseng e le mulch, mme o boloke kutu ya sefate (trunk) e hlakile.
items.blindBackTranslation: Return suitable cut leaves as mulch, and keep the tree trunk clear.

items.sourceEnglish: Bocking 14 does not spread by viable seed, but root pieces can regrow.
items.draft: Bocking 14 ha e phatlalale ka viable seed, empa dikotwana tsa metso di ka mela hape.
items.blindBackTranslation: Bocking 14 ha is propagated by viable seed, but pieces of roots can grow again.

items.sourceEnglish: Flowering plants can support useful insects; watch actual visits and crop damage.
items.draft: Dimela tse nang le dipalesa di ka thusa dikokwanyana (insects) tse molemo; shebisisa ketelo tse hlileng di etsahala le tshenyo ya dijalo.
items.blindBackTranslation: Flowering plants can help beneficial insects; watch the visits that actually happen and the damage to crops.

items.sourceEnglish: What does the branch-cutting clip show?
items.draft: Video ya ho seha lekala e bontsha eng?
items.blindBackTranslation: What does the branch-cutting video show?

items.sourceEnglish: Removing the whole support tree
items.draft: Ho tlosa support tree kaofela
items.blindBackTranslation: Removing the whole support tree

items.sourceEnglish: Pruning a retained support tree for light and mulch
items.draft: Ho faola support tree e bolokilweng bakeng sa lesedi le mulch
items.blindBackTranslation: Pruning a support tree kept for light and mulch

items.sourceEnglish: Harvesting the fruit tree
items.draft: Ho kotula sefate sa ditholwana
items.blindBackTranslation: Harvesting a fruit tree

items.sourceEnglish: Proof that root competition has stopped
items.draft: Bopaki ba hore tlhodisano ya metso e emile
items.blindBackTranslation: Evidence that root competition has stopped

items.sourceEnglish: A branch falls, while the support tree remains standing. That is pruning and chop-and-drop.
items.draft: Lekala le a wa, athe support tree e ntse e eme. Seo ke ho faola le chop-and-drop.
items.blindBackTranslation: A branch falls while the support tree is still standing. That is pruning/cutting back and chop-and-drop.

items.sourceEnglish: How should you assess flowering plants used to support helpful insects?
items.draft: O ka lekola jwang dimela tse nang le dipalesa tse sebediswang ho thusa dikokwanyana (insects) tse molemo?
items.blindBackTranslation: How can you check flowering plants used to help beneficial insects?

items.sourceEnglish: Assume they will eliminate pests
items.draft: Nka hore di tla fedisa dikokwanyana tse senyang (pests)
items.blindBackTranslation: Assume that they will finish off the pests

items.sourceEnglish: Observe insect visitors and changes in crop damage
items.draft: Shebisisa dikokwanyana (insects) tse etelang le diphetoho tshenyong ya dijalo
items.blindBackTranslation: Watch closely the visiting insects and the changes in crop damage

items.sourceEnglish: Remove all flowers before they open
items.draft: Tlosa dipalesa tsohle pele di buleha
items.blindBackTranslation: Remove all flowers before they open

items.sourceEnglish: Count every flowering plant as a nitrogen fixer
items.draft: Bala semela se seng le se seng se nang le dipalesa e le nitrogen fixer
items.blindBackTranslation: Count every plant that has flowers as a nitrogen fixer

items.sourceEnglish: Flowers can supply resources, but their presence does not guarantee pest control.
items.draft: Dipalesa di ka fana ka mehlodi, empa ho ba teng ha tsona ha ho tiise hore dikokwanyana tse senyang (pests) di a laoleha.
items.blindBackTranslation: Flowers can provide resources, but their presence does not guarantee that pests are controlled.

items.sourceEnglish: Combine the support functions your site needs: nitrogen fixation, food, mulch, flowers and ground cover. Some plants serve several functions.
items.draft: Kopanya support functions tseo sebaka sa hao se di hlokang: nitrogen fixation, dijo, mulch, dipalesa le dimela tse kwahelang mobu. Dimela tse ding di sebetsa mesebetsi e mengata.
items.blindBackTranslation: Combine the support functions that your area needs: nitrogen fixation, food, mulch, flowers and ground-cover plants. Some plants perform many functions.

items.sourceEnglish: Keep the trunk area and path open. Reassess each member as the mango and its neighbours grow.
items.draft: Boloka sebaka sa kutu ya sefate (trunk) le tsela di bulehile. Hlahloba hape setho se seng le se seng ha mango le dimela tse haufi le yona di ntse di hola.
items.blindBackTranslation: Keep the trunk area and the access path open. Re-check each member as the mango and nearby plants grow.

items.sourceEnglish: Keep its vines away from the young fruit tree and retain a route for care. Its roots also use water and nutrients.
items.draft: Boloka makala a yona a hasanang (vines) hole le sefate se senyane sa ditholwana, mme o boloke tsela ya tlhokomelo. Metso ya yona le yona e sebedisa metsi le nutrients.
items.blindBackTranslation: Keep its spreading vines away from the young fruit tree, and keep an access path for care. Its roots also use water and nutrients.

items.sourceEnglish: Where resources are tight, compare living cover with an ordinary mulch basin.
items.draft: Moo mehlodi e sa lekaneng, bapisa se kwahelang mobu se phelang le mulch basin e tlwaelehileng.
items.blindBackTranslation: Where resources are not enough, compare a living ground cover with a plain mulch basin.

items.sourceEnglish: Plant into a suitable season, mulch and maintain establishment water. Keep the access gap open.
items.draft: Jala sehleng se loketseng, beha mulch, mme o tswelepele ho nosetsa nakong ya ho thehwa ha semela. Boloka sekgeo sa ho fihlella se bulehile.
items.blindBackTranslation: Plant in a suitable season, put on mulch, and continue to water during the time of the plant's establishment. Keep the access gap open.

items.sourceEnglish: Start with the number of support plants you can care for. Observe survival and growth before adding more.
items.draft: Qala ka palo ya support plants eo o ka e hlokomelang. Shebisisa ho phela le kgolo pele o eketsa tse ding.
items.blindBackTranslation: Start with a number of support plants that you can take care of. Watch survival and growth before you add others.

items.sourceEnglish: Cut down selected competing supports to open space. Suitable cut material can stay as mulch: this is thinning through chop-and-drop.
items.draft: Seha fatshe support plants tse kgethilweng tse tlhodisanang ho bula sebaka. Thepa e sehilweng e loketseng e ka sala e le mulch: sena ke ho fokotsa (thinning) ka chop-and-drop.
items.blindBackTranslation: Cut down selected support plants that compete, to open space. Suitable cut material can stay as mulch: this is thinning by chop-and-drop.

items.sourceEnglish: Manage regrowth to keep the opening. Check light, soil moisture and growth; thinning does not instantly stop root competition.
items.draft: Laola ho mela hape ho boloka sebaka se butsweng. Hlahloba lesedi, mongobo wa mobu le kgolo; ho fokotsa (thinning) ha ho emise hang-hang tlhodisano ya metso.
items.blindBackTranslation: Manage regrowth to keep the opened space. Check light, soil moisture and growth; thinning does not immediately stop root competition.

items.sourceEnglish: Carry useful prunings back to established trees. Keep nearby plants only where they still perform well.
items.draft: Busetsa makala a faotsweng a nang le molemo ho difate tse seng di thehilwe hantle. Boloka dimela tse haufi feela moo di ntseng di sebetsa hantle.
items.blindBackTranslation: Return useful pruned branches to trees not yet well established. Keep nearby plants only where they are working well.

items.sourceEnglish: Mature fruit trees still need nutrients. Monitor growth, harvest and soil conditions; support plants do not remove that need.
items.draft: Difate tse hodileng tsa ditholwana di ntse di hloka nutrients. Shebisisa kgolo, thobo le maemo a mobu; support plants ha di tlose tlhoko eo.
items.blindBackTranslation: Mature fruit trees still need nutrients. Watch growth, harvest and soil conditions; support plants do not remove that need.

items.sourceEnglish: Check fruit-tree growth, shade, soil moisture, useful harvests and pest damage. Note what was cut, returned or removed.
items.draft: Hlahloba kgolo ya sefate sa ditholwana, moriti, mongobo wa mobu, thobo e nang le molemo le tshenyo ya dikokwanyana tse senyang (pests). Ngola seo se sehilweng, se kgutlisitsweng kapa se tlositsweng.
items.blindBackTranslation: Check the fruit tree's growth, shade, soil moisture, useful yield and pest damage. Record what was cut, returned or removed.

items.sourceEnglish: Use these observations to change the layout and care. A plant earns its place through what it does here.
items.draft: Sebedisa dintho tsena tseo o di shebisisitseng ho fetola moralo le tlhokomelo. Semela se tshwanelwa ke sebaka sa sona ka lebaka la seo se se etsang mona.
items.blindBackTranslation: Use these things that you have examined closely to change the design and the care. A plant deserves its place because of what it does here.

items.sourceEnglish: Conceptual guild teaching illustration; confirm plant identity with reliable botanical guidance.
items.draft: Setshwantsho sa mohopolo sa ho ruta ka guild; netefatsa hore semela ke sefe ka botanical guidance e tshepehang.
items.blindBackTranslation: Concept picture for teaching about a guild; confirm which plant it is using reliable botanical guidance.

items.sourceEnglish: Build a Guild and Adjust It as It Grows
items.draft: Haha sehlopha sa dimela (guild), mme o se fetole ha se ntse se hola
items.blindBackTranslation: Build a group of plants (guild), and change it as it grows

items.sourceEnglish: Give each plant a useful role while protecting the fruit tree's space.
items.draft: Fa semela ka seng mosebetsi o molemo, empa o sireletse sebaka sa sefate sa ditholwana.
items.blindBackTranslation: Give each plant a good job, but protect the fruit tree's space.

items.sourceEnglish: Living ground cover also competes for water and nutrients.
items.draft: Dimela tse phelang tse kwahelang mobu le tsona di tlhodisana le tse ding bakeng sa metsi le nutrients.
items.blindBackTranslation: Living ground-cover plants also compete with others for water and nutrients.

items.sourceEnglish: Thin selected whole support plants when pruning no longer gives enough room.
items.draft: Ha ho faola ho se ho sa fane ka sebaka se lekaneng, etsa thinning ka ho tlosa ka botlalo support plants tse kgethilweng.
items.blindBackTranslation: When pruning no longer gives enough space, thin by removing selected support plants completely.

items.sourceEnglish: Suitable cut biomass can stay as mulch; manage regrowth to retain the opening.
items.draft: Biomass e sehilweng e loketseng e ka sala e le mulch; laola ho mela hape hore sebaka se dule se bulehile.
items.blindBackTranslation: Suitable cut biomass can remain as mulch; manage regrowth so that the space stays open.

items.sourceEnglish: A support plant still crowds the mango after pruning. What can thinning involve?
items.draft: Support plant e ntse e pitlaganya mango ka mora ho faola. Ho fokotsa (thinning) ho ka akarelletsa eng?
items.blindBackTranslation: A support plant is still crowding the mango after pruning. What could thinning include?

items.sourceEnglish: Only cutting another small twig
items.draft: Ho seha feela lekala le leng le lenyane
items.blindBackTranslation: Cutting only one small branch

items.draft: Ela hloko dikokwanyana (insects) tse thusang
items.blindBackTranslation: Take note of helpful insects

items.sourceEnglish: Many ladybirds eat aphids; some parasitoid wasps attack crop pests. Flowering members such as African basil can add resources.  Watch which insects visit and whether damage changes. A flowering plant does not guarantee pest control. What is the insect actually doing?
items.draft: Ladybirds tse ngata di ja aphids; parasitoid wasps tse ding di hlasela dikokwanyana tse senyang dijalo (pests). Ditho tse nang le dipalesa tse kang African basil di ka eketsa mehlodi. Shebisisa hore ke dikokwanyana (insects) dife tse etelang le hore na tshenyo e a fetoha. Semela se nang le dipalesa ha se tiise ho laolwa ha dikokwanyana tse senyang (pests). Kokwanyana eo ka nnete e etsa eng?
items.blindBackTranslation: Many ladybirds eat aphids; some parasitoid wasps attack insects that damage crops (pests). Flowering members such as African basil can add resources. Check which insects (insects) visit and whether the damage changes. A flowering plant does not guarantee control of damaging insects (pests). What does that insect actually do?

items.sourceEnglish: Give Flowers Their Space
items.draft: Fa dipalesa sebaka sa tsona
items.blindBackTranslation: Give flowers their place

items.sourceEnglish: Wild garlic can be a flowering member where the site suits it.
items.draft: Wild garlic e ka ba setho se nang le dipalesa moo sebaka se e loketseng.
items.blindBackTranslation: Wild garlic can be a member that has flowers where the place suits it.

items.sourceEnglish: Give Flowers Their Space
items.draft: Fa dipalesa sebaka sa tsona
items.blindBackTranslation: Give flowers their place

items.sourceEnglish: Tulbaghia violacea has narrow leaves and lilac flowers. Place a clump where it has light and room to grow.  Observe visiting insects. Do not promise that a ring of wild garlic will repel pests or cure an outbreak. Where can flowers grow without crowding?
items.draft: Tulbaghia violacea e na le mahlaku a masesane le dipalesa tse mmala wa lilac. Bea sehlopha sa yona moo se nang le lesedi le sebaka sa ho hola. Shebisisa dikokwanyana (insects) tse etelang. O se ke wa tshepisa hore sedikadikwe (ring) sa wild garlic se tla leleka dikokwanyana tse senyang (pests) kapa hore se tla fedisa ho phatlalala ho kgolo ha tsona. Dipalesa di ka mela kae ntle le ho pitlagana?
items.blindBackTranslation: Tulbaghia violacea has narrow leaves and lilac-coloured flowers. Place its group where there is light and room to grow. Watch the insects (insects) that visit. Do not promise that a ring (ring) of wild garlic will drive away pests (pests) or that it will stop their spread or growth. Where can the flowers grow without crowding?

items.sourceEnglish: Bring the Jobs Together
items.draft: Kopanya mesebetsi mmoho
items.blindBackTranslation: Combine functions together

items.sourceEnglish: Choose useful partners while protecting the mango's growing space.
items.draft: Kgetha balekane ba thusang ha o ntse o sireletsa sebaka sa ho hola sa mango.
items.blindBackTranslation: Choose partners that help while protecting the mango's growing space.

items.sourceEnglish: Bring the Jobs Together
items.draft: Kopanya mesebetsi mmoho
items.blindBackTranslation: Combine functions together

items.sourceEnglish: Combine the support functions your site needs: nitrogen fixation, food, mulch, flowers and ground cover. Some plants serve several functions.  Keep the trunk area and path open. Reassess each member as the mango and its neighbours grow. Does each member have space and a job?
items.draft: Kopanya support functions tseo sebaka sa hao se di hlokang: nitrogen fixation, dijo, mulch, dipalesa le dimela tse kwahelang mobu. Dimela tse ding di sebetsa mesebetsi e mengata. Boloka sebaka sa kutu ya sefate (trunk) le tsela di bulehile. Hlahloba hape setho se seng le se seng ha mango le dimela tse haufi le yona di ntse di hola. Na setho ka seng se na le sebaka hammoho le mosebetsi?
items.blindBackTranslation: Combine the support functions that your site needs: nitrogen fixation, food, mulch, flowers and ground-cover plants. Some plants perform many functions. Keep the trunk (trunk) area and the path open. Check again each member, the mango and the plants near it, as they grow. Does each member have both space and a function?

items.sourceEnglish: Food Cover Also Competes
items.draft: Sekwahelo sa dijo le sona se a tlhodisana
items.blindBackTranslation: A food cover/ground cover also competes

items.sourceEnglish: Sweet potato can cover ground and provide food in a suitable sunny space.
items.draft: Sweet potato e ka kwahela mobu le ho fana ka dijo sebakeng se loketseng se nang le letsatsi.
items.blindBackTranslation: Sweet potato can cover the soil and provide food in a suitable sunny area.

items.sourceEnglish: Food Cover Also Competes
items.draft: Sekwahelo sa dijo le sona se a tlhodisana
items.blindBackTranslation: A food cover/ground cover also competes

items.sourceEnglish: Keep its vines away from the young fruit tree and retain a route for care. Its roots also use water and nutrients.  Where resources are tight, compare living cover with an ordinary mulch basin. Is this cover helping the tree establish?
items.draft: Boloka makala a yona a hasanang (vines) hole le sefate se senyane sa ditholwana, mme o boloke tsela ya tlhokomelo. Metso ya yona le yona e sebedisa metsi le nutrients. Moo mehlodi e sa lekaneng, bapisa se kwahelang mobu se phelang le mulch basin e tlwaelehileng. Na sekwahelo sena se thusa sefate ho thehwa hantle (establishment)?
items.blindBackTranslation: Keep its spreading branches (vines) away from the young fruit tree, and keep an access path for care. Its roots also use water and nutrients. Where resources are not enough, compare a living ground cover with an ordinary mulch basin. Does this cover help the tree to establish well (establishment)?

items.sourceEnglish: First, Establish the Guild
items.draft: Pele, theha guild
items.blindBackTranslation: First, create the guild

items.sourceEnglish: Start while the young fruit tree and its support plants have enough light and water.
items.draft: Qala ha sefate sa ditholwana se senyane le support plants tsa sona di na le lesedi le metsi a lekaneng.
items.blindBackTranslation: Start when the small fruit tree and its support plants have enough light and water.

items.sourceEnglish: First, Establish the Guild
items.draft: Pele, theha guild
items.blindBackTranslation: First, create the guild

items.sourceEnglish: Plant into a suitable season, mulch and maintain establishment water. Keep the access gap open.  Start with the number of support plants you can care for. Observe survival and growth before adding more. Can you care for every plant through establishment?
items.draft: Jala sehleng se loketseng, beha mulch, mme o tswelepele ho nosetsa nakong ya ho thehwa ha semela. Boloka sekgeo sa ho fihlella se bulehile. Qala ka palo ya support plants eo o ka e hlokomelang. Shebisisa ho phela le kgolo pele o eketsa tse ding. Na o ka kgona ho hlokomela semela se seng le se seng ho fihlela se thehilwe hantle?
items.blindBackTranslation: Plant in a suitable season, put on mulch, and keep watering during plant establishment. Keep the access gap open. Start with the number of support plants that you can look after. Watch survival and growth before adding more. Can you look after each plant until it is well established?

items.sourceEnglish: Thin as the Fruit Tree Grows
items.draft: Thinning ha sefate sa ditholwana se hola
items.blindBackTranslation: Thinning as the fruit tree grows

items.sourceEnglish: When pruning is no longer enough, reduce selected support plants. Cut down selected competing supports to open space. Suitable cut material can stay as mulch: this is thinning through chop-and-drop.  Manage regrowth to keep the opening. Check light, soil moisture and growth; thinning does not instantly stop root competition. Which support plants should now give way?
items.draft: Ha ho faola ho se ho sa lekana, fokotsa support plants tse kgethilweng. Seha fatshe support plants tse kgethilweng tse tlhodisanang ho bula sebaka. Thepa e sehilweng e loketseng e ka sala e le mulch: sena ke ho fokotsa (thinning) ka chop-and-drop. Laola ho mela hape ho boloka sebaka se butsweng. Hlahloba lesedi, mongobo wa mobu le kgolo; ho fokotsa (thinning) ha ho emise hang-hang tlhodisano ya metso. Ke support plants dife tse lokelang ho tlohela sebaka jwale?
items.blindBackTranslation: When pruning is no longer enough, reduce the chosen support plants. Cut down the competing chosen support plants to open up space. Suitable cut material can stay as mulch: this is thinning (thinning) by chop-and-drop. Manage regrowth to keep the opened space. Check light, soil moisture and growth; thinning (thinning) does not immediately stop root competition. Which support plants should give up space now?

items.sourceEnglish: Move Support Into the Light
items.draft: Isa support plants leseding
items.blindBackTranslation: Take support plants to the light

items.sourceEnglish: As shade increases, renew sun-loving support plants in open edges and younger plantings.
items.draft: Ha moriti o eketseha, ntjhafatsa support plants tse ratang letsatsi mahlakoreng a bulehileng le dijalong tse ntjha.
items.blindBackTranslation: As shade increases, renew the sun-loving support plants on the open sides and in new plantings.

items.sourceEnglish: Move Support Into the Light
items.draft: Isa support plants leseding
items.blindBackTranslation: Take support plants to the light

items.sourceEnglish: Carry useful prunings back to established trees. Keep nearby plants only where they still perform well.  Mature fruit trees still need nutrients. Monitor growth, harvest and soil conditions; support plants do not remove that need. Where is the next useful sunny space?
items.draft: Busetsa makala a faotsweng a nang le molemo ho difate tse seng di thehilwe hantle. Boloka dimela tse haufi feela moo di ntseng di sebetsa hantle. Difate tse hodileng tsa ditholwana di ntse di hloka nutrients. Shebisisa kgolo, thobo le maemo a mobu; support plants ha di tlose tlhoko eo. Sebaka se latelang se nang le letsatsi se thusang ke kae?
items.blindBackTranslation: Return useful pruned branches to trees that are already well established. Keep nearby plants only where they are still working well. Mature fruit trees still need nutrients. Watch growth, yield and soil conditions; support plants do not remove that need. Where is the next sunny place that helps?

items.sourceEnglish: Let Observation Decide
items.draft: Etsa qeto ka seo o se bonang
items.blindBackTranslation: Make a decision about what you see

items.sourceEnglish: Keep a short record of how the guild performs.
items.draft: Boloka rekoto e kgutshwane ya kamoo guild e sebetsang kateng.
items.blindBackTranslation: Keep a short record of how the guild is working.

items.sourceEnglish: Let Observation Decide
items.draft: Etsa qeto ka seo o se bonang
items.blindBackTranslation: Make a decision about what you see

items.sourceEnglish: Check fruit-tree growth, shade, soil moisture, useful harvests and pest damage. Note what was cut, returned or removed.  Use these observations to change the layout and care. A plant earns its place through what it does here. What evidence would make you change the guild?
items.draft: Hlahloba kgolo ya sefate sa ditholwana, moriti, mongobo wa mobu, thobo e nang le molemo le tshenyo ya dikokwanyana tse senyang (pests). Ngola seo se sehilweng, se kgutlisitsweng kapa se tlositsweng. Sebedisa dintho tsena tseo o di shebisisitseng ho fetola moralo le tlhokomelo. Semela se tshwanelwa ke sebaka sa sona ka lebaka la seo se se etsang mona. Ke bopaki bofe bo ka o etsang hore o fetole guild?
items.blindBackTranslation: Check the fruit tree's growth, shade, soil moisture, useful yield and damage from damaging insects (pests). Write down what was cut, returned or removed. Use these things you have observed to change the design and care. A plant deserves its place because of what it does here. What evidence could make you change the guild?

items.sourceEnglish: Plan One Real Guild
items.draft: Rala guild e le nngwe ya sebele
items.blindBackTranslation: Design one real guild

items.sourceEnglish: Choose one fruit tree and mark a layout you can manage.
items.draft: Kgetha sefate se le seng sa ditholwana mme o tshwaye moralo oo o ka kgonang ho o laola.
items.blindBackTranslation: Choose one fruit tree and mark the design that you can manage.

items.sourceEnglish: Plan One Real Guild
items.draft: Rala guild e le nngwe ya sebele
items.blindBackTranslation: Design one real guild

items.sourceEnglish: Record the tree, site conditions and missing jobs. Name the support species fully, mark the starting number and leave access.  Write down what will trigger pruning or thinning. Agree the species list with the project team where required. Can someone else explain your plan back to you?
items.draft: Ngola sefate, maemo a sebaka le mesebetsi e haellang. Reha support species ka botlalo, o tshwaye palo ya ho qala mme o siye tsela ya ho fihlella. Ngola seo se tla susumetsa ho faola kapa thinning. Dumellana ka lenane la mefuta le sehlopha sa porojeke moo ho hlokahalang. Na ho na le motho e mong ya ka kgonang ho o hlalosetsa leano la hao hape?
items.blindBackTranslation: Record the tree, site conditions and missing functions. Name the support species fully, mark the starting number and leave an access path. Record what will prompt pruning or thinning. Agree a species list with the project team where needed. Is there anyone else who can explain your plan again?

items.sourceEnglish: Plant, Observe, Adjust
items.draft: Jala, shebella, fetola
items.blindBackTranslation: Plant, watch, change

items.sourceEnglish: Start one suitable guild and care for it through its first stage.
items.draft: Qala guild e le nngwe e loketseng mme o e hlokomele mohatong wa yona wa pele.
items.blindBackTranslation: Start one suitable guild and look after it in its first stage.

items.sourceEnglish: Plant, Observe, Adjust
items.draft: Jala, shebella, fetola
items.blindBackTranslation: Plant, watch, change

items.sourceEnglish: Use the right species, a manageable number of plants and room to grow. Return useful biomass and protect the fruit tree.  Review the planting as crowns expand. Keep, cut, replace or remove each support plant when its role changes. What will you do first—and when will you review it?
items.draft: Sebedisa mefuta e nepahetseng, palo ya dimela e ka laolwang le sebaka sa ho hola. Kgutlisetsa biomass e thusang mme o sireletse sefate sa ditholwana. Hlahloba jalo hape ha crowns di ntse di hola. Boloka, seha, ntjhafatsa kapa tlosa support plant ka nngwe ha mosebetsi wa yona o fetoha. O tla etsa eng pele, mme o tla e hlahloba neng?
items.blindBackTranslation: Use suitable species, a manageable number of plants and room to grow. Return helpful biomass and protect the fruit tree. Check the planting again as the crowns grow. Keep, cut back, renew or remove each support plant when its function changes. What will you do first, and when will you check it?
